newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Tanzanian bourse body approves brokerage firms.
newsitem.headline: Tanzanian bourse body approves brokerage firms.

text.p: Tanzania's embryonic Capital Markets and Securities Authority (CMSA) on Wednesday said it had approved and licensed five stock broker/dealers to trade at the country's yet-to-be-opened stock exchange.

"The licensing excercise constitutes and important milestone in the establishment of the Dar es Salaam Stock Exchange (DSE) as the council of the exchange can now be formed," CMSA said."The formation of the council will in turn pave the way for the operationalisation of the exchange."
Last week a senior CMSA official said he expected trading, put back by more than a year, to start within three months.
The five companies, chosen from a list of 17 applicants, are Tanzania Securities Ltd, Exim Securities and Investments Co Ltd, Rasilimali Ltd, Solomon and Co Ltd and Orbit Securities Co Ltd.
The CMSA said the licenses were provisional pending compliance with holders meeting a minimum capital requirement.
The CMSA Act of 1994 allows a dual capacity license for dealers who may deal on their own account as principal, bearing the risk themselves, or as an agent handling client accounts.

For dealers, the minimum level of capitalisation is 20 million Tanzanian shillings ($32,300) and for brokers (single capacity) 10 million shillings. The CMSA said the capitalisation requirement may be reviewed after the opening of the DSE.
Licensing criteria for securities dealers disallowed foreign companies or companies with foreign shareholding until an in-depth study on foreign participation in the Tanzanian market is carried out.
"It is recognised that foreign dealers will bring with them technology as well as skills which will benefit the Tanzania market," the CMSA said.

"However, the modalities of their participation needs to be worked out so that a framework is laid for local dealers as well as the market to gain the most benefit of foreign dealers participation," the CMSA added.

The Council of the DSE will comprise three licensed dealers, two associate members from listed companies, one associate member from an institutional investor, two associate members representing the profession and oneassociate member from the public. The DSE Council will be headed by a chief executive.

Zebedee Mpogolo, CMSA's director of operations and finance, said last week that the bourse would open for trading in three months. He added that 13 major Tanzanian corporations had been approved for listing on the exchange.

Acknowledging long delays in the opening of the exchange, he said these had been caused mostly by legal problems associated with companies changing their legal framework from private to public for their prospectuses.
